summary: Specifies how members of the IAB and IESG, some IETF Trust trustees, and some IETF LLC directors are selected, confirmed, and recalled through the Nominating and Recall Committees. It is based on RFC 7437 with only the updates required by IASA 2.0, and it obsoletes RFC 7437 and RFC 8318.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC sets out how the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) chooses and confirms members of the Internet Architecture Board (IAB), Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG), IETF Trust, and IETF Administration LLC Board. It also explains how a petition can start a recall process.

questions: how are iab and iesg members chosen
how many volunteers are on the nomcom
subtitle: How the IETF selects and confirms leaders, and how its community can request a recall.

tldr.problem: The IETF needs a defined process for choosing and, when necessary, recalling leaders in several IETF bodies.
tldr.mechanism: A Nominating Committee (NomCom) of ten randomly selected voting volunteers chooses candidates, confirming bodies review them, and a separate recall process investigates petitions.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8713 updates the process for IASA 2.0 and replaces RFC 7437 and RFC 8318. It is BCP 10 and is updated by RFC 9389.

sections.title: Which Positions the Process Covers
sections.content:
RFC 8713 specifies how members of the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) and Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG), some IETF Trust Trustees, and some IETF LLC Directors are selected, confirmed, and recalled. It revises RFC 7437 to reflect the IETF Administrative Support Activity 2.0 structure.

The process does not cover the Internet Research Task Force or the organization of the IESG. Its schedule is framed around the three IETF meetings held in a calendar year.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC covers how several IETF leadership positions are filled and reviewed. It updates the process to account for the IETF's administrative structure.

sections.title: The Annual Selection Cycle
sections.content:
The annual process includes selecting and organizing NomCom members, selecting candidates, and confirming candidates. It is designed to finish within seven months, with an additional month available before new terms begin. Each year, about half of the IESG and IAB positions and one position each in the IETF Trust and IETF LLC are normally reviewed.

NomCom does not choose which positions are open; the relevant bodies identify them and describe the expertise sought. Confirmed IESG and IAB candidates are expected to serve at least two years. IETF Trust Trustees and IETF LLC Directors are expected to serve at least three years, subject to exceptions for initial staggered appointments.

Mid-term vacancies use the same process with a shorter schedule: candidate selection and confirmation are due within six weeks, and the confirming body has two weeks to reject a candidate.
sections.plainLanguage: The process runs on a yearly calendar with separate periods for choosing volunteers, selecting candidates, and confirming them. Each year, the committee reviews a planned set of open positions.

sections.title: Advice, Consent, and Confidentiality
sections.content:
The process generally uses advice and consent. The NomCom recommends one candidate for each open position and explains how each candidate meets the requested qualifications. A confirming body may accept some, all, or none of the candidates; when a candidate is rejected, the NomCom selects an alternate.

Each confirming body uses its own decision rule. If it has no specific rule, confirmation should require agreement from at least half of its sitting members. Deliberations and information about specific nominees and candidates are confidential. The NomCom may disclose the names of willing nominees to seek community feedback, but public campaigning is discouraged.
sections.plainLanguage: The NomCom recommends candidates, but a separate confirming body decides whether each person is approved. Discussions about individual candidates are confidential.

sections.title: Who Serves on the NomCom
sections.content:
The NomCom includes a Chair, ten voting volunteers, liaisons, and advisors. Only the voting volunteers choose candidates. The IAB and IESG appoint liaisons; the IETF Trust and IETF LLC Board may also appoint liaisons. The previous year's Chair serves as an advisor.

A volunteer must have attended at least three of the last five IETF meetings. Members of specified IETF bodies, along with IETF LLC employees and contractors, cannot serve as voting volunteers. No more than two selected volunteers may share the same primary affiliation.

The term is expected to last 15 months, overlapping the next NomCom's term by about three months. During that overlap, the prior year's committee handles mid-term vacancies.
sections.plainLanguage: Ten volunteers vote on candidates, while liaisons and advisors provide information. Attendance and affiliation rules help determine who may serve and how the volunteers are selected.

sections.title: Selecting Volunteers and Candidates
sections.content:
The Chair announces the volunteer pool and selection method before a public random draw. The method must be independently verifiable, fair to eligible volunteers, unbiased, and repeatable if a selected volunteer becomes unavailable. The selected members are announced, with a challenge period of at least one week.

Once formed, the NomCom invites nominations. Any IETF community member may nominate someone or themselves, but a nominee must consent in writing before becoming a candidate. The voting volunteers select candidates after consulting the community. The NomCom sends the confirming body one candidate for each position, along with a statement of qualifications.
sections.plainLanguage: The NomCom, or Nominating Committee, uses a random method that people can check to select its voting volunteers. The committee then considers nominations and sends candidates to the groups that confirm them.

sections.title: Disputes and Recall
sections.content:
When a process dispute cannot be resolved within the NomCom, a written request goes to the Internet Society President, who appoints an arbiter. The arbiter consults the principal parties and issues a final, binding decision with no appeal. The process should finish within two weeks, and the NomCom must not submit candidates while the issue remains unresolved.

A recall request may be submitted for covered IESG, IAB, IETF Trust, and IETF LLC positions. A community petition needs at least 20 qualified signatories and supporting reasons; an Ombudsteam petition follows RFC 7776 and does not need those community signatures. A recall committee investigates, gives the person a chance to provide a written statement, consults third parties, and votes. Recall requires a three-quarters majority of those voting.
sections.plainLanguage: A process dispute can go to an arbiter for a final decision. A recall petition starts a separate investigation, and removal requires a three-quarters majority of votes cast.

sections.title: Confidential Information
sections.content:
The RFC's security considerations focus on protecting information gathered during selection, confirmation, and recall. Participants must keep confidential anything not explicitly identified as suitable for public release.

If the NomCom shares private information with people it consults, it must share only what is needed and obtain their agreement to follow the same confidentiality rules.
sections.plainLanguage: The process can expose private information about nominees and candidates. Participants must protect it and share as little as necessary.
